The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. Job 01a15f9f-3367-7219-a42d-a8debef06420 completed with counts {"00": 56, "11": 44} under key "m". Only the Bell outcomes 00 and 11 appeared.

What I changed and why:
1. I replaced QB25 with QB2. Garnet has only 20 qubits (QB1 to QB20), so QB25 does not exist. The live garnet:mock architecture lists cz pairs for QB1 only with QB2 and QB4. I picked QB2.
2. I replaced "cx" with native gates. "cx" is not a native IQM operation. Garnet accepts only prx, cz and measure. A CNOT equals Ry(-pi/2) on the target, then CZ, then Ry(pi/2) on the target. I wrote that as prx(angle=-pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2, then cz on (QB1, QB2), then prx(angle=pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2. The cz uses the coupler that the architecture lists as ("QB2", "QB1"). CZ is symmetric, so the qubit order inside the pair does not matter.
3. I kept the first prx(pi/2, phase pi/2) on QB1, which is Ry(pi/2). I also kept the single measure on QB1 and QB2 with key "m".

Fixed instructions: prx QB1 (pi/2, pi/2); prx QB2 (-pi/2, pi/2); cz QB2,QB1; prx QB2 (pi/2, pi/2); measure QB1,QB2 key "m".

The mock returns simulated results, so these counts say nothing about real hardware quality. The script is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_3612af23-e49-15/scratch/run_bell_fix.py.
